title: Just a bit of air
setting: A stormy autumn Saturday at Kenta's flat. Yuki and Kenta had planned a bike ride, but the rain and wind have kept them in all day.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: うわあ、雨強くなってきた。
lines.kana: うわあ、あめつよくなってきた。
lines.english: Whoa, the rain's really coming down now.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kaze mo tsuyoi ne. kore ja, jitensha norenai yo.
lines.ja: 風も強いね。これじゃ、自転車乗れないよ。
lines.kana: かぜもつよいね。これじゃ、じてんしゃのれないよ。
lines.english: And it's windy, too. We can't go cycling in this.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kinou wa ii tenki datta noni naa.
lines.ja: 昨日はいい天気だったのになあ。
lines.kana: きのうはいいてんきだったのになあ。
lines.english: And the weather was so nice yesterday.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ashita wa tenki ii tte. jitensha, ashita ni suru?
lines.ja: 明日は天気いいって。自転車、明日にする？
lines.kana: あしたはてんきいいって。じてんしゃ、あしたにする？
lines.english: They say it'll be nice tomorrow. Want to do the bike ride tomorrow instead?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, ashita ni shiyou. kyou wa ame tsuyoi shi.
lines.ja: うん、明日にしよう。今日は雨強いし。
lines.kana: うん、あしたにしよう。きょうはあめつよいし。
lines.english: Yeah, let's make it tomorrow. The rain's so heavy today, anyway.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.english: Why does it stop now, of all times?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: zutto uchi ni ita shi, chotto kaze ni atatte kuru.
lines.ja: ずっとうちにいたし、ちょっと風に当たってくる。
lines.kana: ずっとうちにいたし、ちょっとかぜにあたってくる。
lines.english: I've been stuck inside all day. I'm going to go and get some air.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: でも、まだかぜつよいよ？
lines.english: But it's still windy out, you know.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: daijoubu. aa, ii kaze fuiteru. kimochi ii!
lines.ja: 大丈夫。ああ、いい風吹いてる。気持ちいい！
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。ああ、いいかぜふいてる。きもちいい！
lines.english: I'll be fine. Ahh, there's a lovely breeze. That feels great!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii kaze? tsumetai kaze fuiteru dake da yo.
lines.ja: いい風？冷たい風吹いてるだけだよ。
lines.kana: いいかぜ？つめたいかぜふいてるだけだよ。
lines.english: A lovely breeze? It's just a cold wind blowing.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sore ga ii n da yo.
lines.english: That's what's so nice about it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: zutto kaze ni atatteru to, kaze hiku yo.
lines.ja: ずっと風に当たってると、風邪ひくよ。
lines.kana: ずっとかぜにあたってると、かぜひくよ。
lines.english: Stay out in the wind too long and you'll catch a cold.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: ひかないよ。はっくしょん！
lines.kana: ひかないよ。はっくしょん！

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.english: What, you've caught a cold already?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hiitenai yo. chotto kaze ni atatta dake.
lines.ja: ひいてないよ。ちょっと風に当たっただけ。
lines.kana: ひいてないよ。ちょっとかぜにあたっただけ。
lines.english: I have not. I just got a bit of air.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou, haitte! ashita, jitensha noru n desho?
lines.ja: もう、入って！明日、自転車乗るんでしょ？
lines.kana: もう、はいって！あした、じてんしゃのるんでしょ？
lines.english: Honestly, get back inside! We're cycling tomorrow, aren't we?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai hai. ashita, tenki ii to ii na.
lines.ja: はいはい。明日、天気いいといいな。
lines.kana: はいはい。あした、てんきいいといいな。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Hope the weather's nice tomorrow.

choices.english: The rain stops, so they go out on their bikes after all, wind or no wind.
Yuki goes out for some air in the cold wind, and Kenta warns her she'll catch a cold.
They put the bike ride off until tomorrow, and Kenta stands out in the cold wind and starts sneezing.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: the rain is heavy and it's windy too, so they can't ride (jitensha norenai). Lines 4-5: the weather is supposed to be nice tomorrow, so they move the ride to tomorrow (ashita ni shiyou). Line 6: the rain stops, but it's still windy (line 9). Line 8: Kenta goes out to get some air (kaze ni atatte kuru). Lines 11-13: Yuki says it's a cold wind and warns him he'll catch a cold, and in line 14 he sneezes (hakkushon). A is wrong: the ride stays tomorrow's plan (line 17: ashita, jitensha noru n desho?), and the wind is still strong (line 9). B swaps the two of them: Kenta is the one who goes out (line 8), and Yuki gives the warning (line 13).

questions.english: It's a bright, sunny morning. Your elderly neighbour Satou-san greets you in the street: "ohayou gozaimasu." Greet him back and say what nice weather it is.
questions.answer: Greet him and remark on the weather with ii tenki, made polite with o- and desu: ohayou gozaimasu. ii otenki desu ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. ii otenki desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。いいお天気ですね。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. Lovely weather, isn't it?

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kyou wa tenki ga ii desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。今日は天気がいいですね。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. The weather's nice today, isn't it?

questions.explanation: Nice weather is ii tenki, or tenki ga ii; English 'beautiful weather' pushes kirei na tenki, which sounds odd. Yuki and Kenta use it casually in lines 3, 4 and 18 (kinou wa ii tenki datta noni naa / ashita wa tenki ii tte / tenki ii to ii na). To an older neighbour like Satou-san, add o- and desu: ii otenki desu ne is the standard remark after a morning greeting. Both models are polite: the first puts ii before the noun, the second uses the tenki ga ii pattern.

questions.english: Kenta says he's going out to get some air. What does Yuki say back?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: But it's still raining hard, you know.
But it's still windy, you know.
But the wind's still high, you know.

questions.explanation: Line 9: demo, mada kaze tsuyoi yo? Japanese has no adjective for 'windy': you say the wind is strong, kaze ga tsuyoi, with ga dropped in casual talk. A is the same frame with ame, which they used in lines 1 and 5, but the rain had just stopped (line 6: a, ame yanda), so it doesn't fit this moment. C turns English 'high winds' into Japanese word for word; takai means high, tall or expensive and is not used of wind.

questions.english: It's pouring where you are. Kenta calls you: "ima kara jitensha de iku ne!" (I'm heading over on my bike now!) Warn him that the rain's heavy.
questions.ja: 今から自転車で行くね！
questions.kana: いまからじてんしゃでいくね！
questions.romaji: ima kara jitensha de iku ne!
questions.answer: Warn him with ame (ga) tsuyoi: e, ame tsuyoi yo!

modelAnswers.romaji: e, ame tsuyoi yo! jitensha wa dame da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、雨強いよ！自転車はだめだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Wait, the rain's really heavy! No bike today.

modelAnswers.romaji: ame, metcha tsuyoku natte kita yo. densha de kite.
modelAnswers.ja: 雨、めっちゃ強くなってきたよ。電車で来て。
modelAnswers.english: The rain's really coming down now. Take the train.

questions.explanation: Heavy rain is strong rain: ame ga tsuyoi, not omoi ame, because omoi is only about weight. Tsuyoku natte kita is 'it's getting heavier', Yuki's opener in line 1; line 5 has the plain form (kyou wa ame tsuyoi shi). In line 2 Kenta answers in the same frame about the wind (kaze mo tsuyoi ne), and between them that's what puts the bike ride off.

questions.english: When Kenta steps outside, he says "aa, ii kaze fuiteru." What does he mean?

choices.english: There's a nice breeze blowing, and he's enjoying it.
The wind has died down at last, so it's calm outside.
He's caught a slight cold, but he feels fine.

questions.explanation: Line 10: ii kaze fuiteru is 'a nice wind is blowing', a breeze. Fuku (fuiteru) is what wind does, and kimochi ii right after says he's enjoying it. Yuki uses the same verb to disagree in line 11 (tsumetai kaze fuiteru dake da yo: it's just a cold wind blowing). B is wrong: fuiteru means the wind is blowing right now, not dying down, and Yuki has just said it's still windy (line 9). C mixes up kaze (wind) with kaze (a cold), which sound the same: only the verb tells them apart. Fuku goes with the wind; a cold takes hiku, as in lines 13 and 15 (kaze hiku yo / mou kaze hiita no?).

questions.english: You're at a crowded party at Kenta's flat, and the room is hot and stuffy. You head for the door, and Kenta asks, "doko iku no?" (Where are you going?) Tell him you're just going to get some air.
questions.answer: Say you're going to let the breeze hit you and come back, with kaze ni ataru + kuru: chotto kaze ni atatte kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto kaze ni atatte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと風に当たってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Just going to get some air.

modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと風に当たってきます。
modelAnswers.english: I'm just going to get some air.

questions.explanation: Nothing in 'get some air' leads to ataru: in Japanese you let the wind hit you, kaze ni ataru, and -te kuru adds 'and come back'. That's Kenta's line 8 (chotto kaze ni atatte kuru), and he says it again in line 16 (chotto kaze ni atatta dake). Keep the ni. Don't confuse it with kaze o hiku: that kaze is a cold, as in Yuki's warning in line 13 (zutto kaze ni atatteru to, kaze hiku yo). The second model is the polite version, for a work party with Tanaka-san.

newWords.english: they say, I heard (passing on news or a forecast: ashita wa tenki ii tte = they say it'll be nice tomorrow)
cold (to the touch); tsumetai kaze = a cold wind
just, only (kaze ni atatta dake = I just got some air)
catch a cold; this kaze (風邪) is a cold and sounds exactly like kaze (風), wind
say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did they say?)
